records.found: On 2026-11-05 a completed, open-label (no sham or placebo) fisetin trial in healthy volunteers was first posted on the registry (NCT07918261, no results); it has no placebo arm, so it does not meet the test. Nothing new on the eye drug UBX1325 or on the Amsterdam liver trial (registry entry NCT05506488 last updated 2026-04-15, no results posted there).

Registry entry for the Amsterdam dasatinib and quercetin liver trial last updated; no results posted on the registry.
Registry entry for the UBX1325 eye trial has posted results (unchanged; no later update).

records.found: On 2026-11-06 Nature Aging published a mouse study reporting that a mineral supplement, vanadyl sulfate, clears aged cells and extends lifespan in male mice. It is another animal result, not a human trial, so it does not meet the test; it is not in the records.

findings.what: Nature Aging paper: oral vanadyl sulfate acts on aged cells, improves age-related conditions and extends lifespan in male mice (abstract read on Europe PMC).

records.found: On 2026-11-02 Immorta Bio announced by press release the first person treated (on 2026-10-29, in Mexico) with SenoMune-0257, an investigational peptide immunotherapy meant to help the immune system remove aged cells; the patient had advanced cancer. It is not an engineered-cell therapy, reports no outcome and gives no registry number, so it does not meet this test; it is a company's own first-human claim worth the author's eye.

findings.what: Immorta Bio (PR Newswire, 08:32 ET) says SenoMune-0257 was first given to one patient with advanced cancer on 2026-10-29 at Integrative Cancer Centers of America in Mexico, in an investigator-run study; no outcomes, no registry number; release says safety and effect are not established.
